title: Friction Diagnostics Record
description: Canonical schema for the friction stream. One append-only JSONL file holds three record kinds: 'friction' (full capture of a genuine surprise), 'recurrence' (cheap pointer to a prior event that bit again), and 'resolution' (provenance that the model mended or closed events). Records without a 'kind' are v4 friction events and remain readable. Records with schema_version below 5.1.0 lack 'decision' and remain readable. Lifecycle is derived, never mutated: an event is open iff its id (or its recurs-anchor) appears in no resolution's 'resolves'.

event_id.description: Unique record identifier (evt-NNNN), auto-generated sequentially per events file

recorded_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of record creation

schema_version.description: Schema version stamped at write time (absent on v4 records)

kind.description: Record kind. Absent means v4 friction event.

session_ref.description: Opaque harness session reference when available (env probe: FRICTION_SESSION_REF, CLAUDE_SESSION_ID, CODEX_SESSION_ID, CODEX_THREAD_ID). On Claude Code an optional plugin SessionStart hook exports FRICTION_SESSION_REF per session; absent hooks, records simply omit this field. Links a record to the transcript where the actual reasoning lives.

events_file.description: Canonical path to the events.jsonl file this record belongs to

repo_root.description: Absolute path to the repository root

actual_outcome.description: What actually happened — verbatim error message, exit code, output, or the sentence as written. Never paraphrase.
actual_outcome.x-eliciting-question: What actually happened? Paste it verbatim — the error text, the output, the sentence as written. No paraphrase.

expected_outcome.description: What the agent predicted would happen and what specifically grounded that prediction
expected_outcome.x-eliciting-question: What did you predict would happen, and what specifically made you predict that?

reading.description: First-person account from inside the decision: what was consulted, what it was believed to say, what was done, and the moment reality diverged from the agent's model of it
reading.x-eliciting-question: Walk through it from inside the decision: what did you consult? What exactly did you believe it said? What did you do? At what moment did reality diverge from your model of it?

decision.description: The response as history: options seen, options set aside, the action actually taken (even 'continued unchanged'), and — for any deviation from a documented mandate — the license the agent operated under at the moment of choice. Past tense; never a proposal.
decision.x-eliciting-question: What did you do about it? Name the options you saw, the ones you set aside, and the action you took — including 'continued unchanged' when true. If your path cut against anything documented as required, state what made that feel permitted at the moment you chose. This is history — the response you made, not the one you would make now.

pivot_information.description: The single piece of information that, had it been visible before acting, would have changed the outcome — or, for friction caught before harm, the fact a future agent should check first. Includes where that information lives, or whether it exists at all. Escape hatch when genuinely unknowable: 'none — the outcome was unknowable in advance, because ...'
pivot_information.x-eliciting-question: Name the single piece of information that, had it been visible before you acted, would have changed the outcome — or, when you caught this before harm, the fact a future agent should check first, or which source should yield. Where does that information actually live — or does it exist anywhere at all?

kind.description: What was trusted: artifact (file/url/doc with a mendable text body), instruction (user/system/skill directive), tool (tool or command behavior), assumption (belief with no external backing), memory (recalled from training or a prior session), observation (something read from output/screen/audio)

ref.description: Path, URL, tool name, or a short label naming the belief

claim.description: What the agent believed it said or would do — verbatim quote for artifact/instruction; the believed proposition for tool/assumption/memory/observation. The prior belief only — never what it turned out to say.

type.description: DEPRECATED v4 field; coerced to 'kind' on write (file|url|documentation→artifact, conversation→instruction, audio|visual→observation, other→other)

excerpt.description: DEPRECATED v4 field; coerced to 'claim' on write

sources.description: What the agent trusted that betrayed it. Each entry names one trusted thing and the claim believed about it.
sources.x-eliciting-question: What did you trust that betrayed you? For each: what kind of thing is it, what is it, and what did you believe it said or would do — the belief exactly as you held it before acting. What it actually turned out to say or do belongs in actual_outcome, never in the claim.

impact.description: How the friction affected the agent's ability to continue. blocked=work stopped, degraded=workaround used, noisy=extra retries/effort, continued=no workflow disruption. On recurrence records, defaults to the anchor event's impact.

recurrence_key.description: Stable 2-5 word hyphenated trap name the agent would use again if this bites again (e.g. 'zsh-status-readonly'). Script computes a content-token fallback (auto- prefix) when omitted. No date component — cross-day recurrence is the signal.
recurrence_key.x-eliciting-question: Name this trap in 2-5 hyphenated words — a stable slug you would use again if it bites again. Omit if unsure.

tags.description: Specific, natural labels as-filed. Normalized to lowercase on write.

title.description: Short human-readable summary; auto-derived from actual_outcome when omitted (preferred). If supplied, composed last.

recurs.description: recurrence records: event_id of the anchor friction event that bit again

note.description: Free slot. On friction records: whatever mattered that no field asked for — deliberately no eliciting question. On recurrence/resolution records: optional short note (what differed this time; context for the resolution).

resolves.description: resolution records: event_ids of the friction events this resolution closes (their recurrences close with them)

action.description: resolution records: what the model did to mend (or 'wontfix: ...' for honest closure of noise). The model resolves; this field only records that it happened.

ref.description: resolution records: provenance pointer — commit, path, or URL of the mend

fingerprint.description: DEPRECATED v4 recurrence hash (hash(source_ref|date)). Read-side grouping uses (.recurrence_key // .fingerprint).

hindsight.description: DEPRECATED v4 field; --hindsight input is coerced to pivot_information on write. Retained so text queries still search the v4 corpus.

aliases.description: DEPRECATED v4 field; alias input is folded into tags on write. Retained so alias queries still work over the v4 corpus.
